newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares leap as U.S. send mild prices signal.
newsitem.headline: German shares leap as U.S. send mild prices signal.

text.p: German shares leapt higher in post-bourse dealings on Tuesday, springing into action after a weak bourse session on the back of a report signalling minimal inflation pressure in the U.S.

The 30-share IBIS DAX index, which monitors all-day electronic trade in blue-chip stocks, surged past the magic 3,000 point level mid-afternoon and ended the day up 35.72 points at 3,028.27, almost 50 points above the day's low.
March DTB DAX futures closed up 38 points at 3,043.
Earlier, the DAX index had ended an edgy floor session down 5.20 points at 2,989.33, weighed upon by profit-taking on bank stocks, its recent outperformers.
The turnaround, which dealers conceded was largely driven by short-covering, came on a report showing lower-than-expected 0.8 percent growth in U.S. fourth quarter labour costs.
"These are really important numbers," one dealer said.

"Alan Greenspan (Federal Reserve chairman) said that if there were to be pressure on prices, it would come from labour costs. This is really good news and it's great to see a lot of the fear taken out of this market," he added.

Bank shares pared their losses on the news having slumped after Commerzbank released a disappointing net profit figure for 1996 in the early morning. Commerzbank ended the late electronic session down 82 pfennigs at 42.87 marks, having closed the bourse session at 42.40.
Deutsche Bank, which announced an unchanged 1996 dividend ended the day down 57 pfennigs at 84.65 marks, after closing the bourse session at 83.30.
Commerzbank reported 1996 profit of around 1.19 billion marks, below analysts' forecasts for 1.3 billion marks.
A Financial Times comment advising taking profits on German bank shares and Moody's move to downgrade Japanese banks this week were adding to pressure on bank shares.

Meanwhile, dollar-sensitive Daimler-Benz rapidly extended its gains to close up 2.85 at 116.10 marks, adding two marks or nearly two percent in afternoon trade. The share had been firm all day as the dollar traded above 1.65 against the mark.
